headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage: Dify can ingest shared workspace content while Perplexity uploads documents and browses externally.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem and uses uploaded knowledge base files, while Perplexity analyzes uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if Dify outputs are fed into Perplexity or vice versa. The pair lacks a documented provenance barrier, so the interaction is not provably blocked.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are copied into Perplexity prompts or uploaded documents
IF Perplexity browsing results are re-ingested by Dify as trusted instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all cross-agent text before reuse
Strip instructions from retrieved documents before passing them onward
Use a human review step for any agent-generated prompt text
Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
requires-engineering: enforce content-type tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets such as model provider API keys; Perplexity touches uploaded documents and browsing context and sends queries to vendor-only APIs. If the pair shares a workspace or copied artifacts, sensitive Dify data can flow into Perplexity’s external backend, creating exfiltration risk in default use.
conditions: IF Dify conversation logs or knowledge base files are reused in Perplexity prompts
IF Perplexity uploads documents that contain Dify secrets or internal content
mitigations: Do not pass secrets or logs from Dify into Perplexity
Use redaction before any cross-agent transfer
Restrict Perplexity to non-sensitive public documents
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: isolate shared storage by tenant

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has broad filesystem write and shell execution, while Perplexity has browser execution and vendor-only network egress. They do not both write the same mutable resource by profile, but they can still contend over shared documents or copied outputs if orchestrated together. Uncertainty about shared storage pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same shared directory or document set
IF one agent’s edits are expected to be authoritative without locking
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Serialize handoffs through a queue
Use file locks for shared artifacts
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Perplexity produces cited answers from browsing context, and Dify can wire tools into agent or workflow apps that may act on upstream text. If Dify consumes Perplexity output as authoritative, a hallucination or citation error can cascade into downstream actions or stored knowledge. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles.
conditions: IF Dify workflows treat Perplexity answers as ground truth
IF downstream Dify tools act on Perplexity-generated facts without verification
mitigations: Require source checking before any action
Keep Perplexity output read-only in Dify
Add a second independent verifier
Log provenance for every imported claim
requires-engineering: implement citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets, while Perplexity handles uploaded documents and browsing context under vendor-only egress. If regulated or internal data is moved from Dify into Perplexity, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated data from Dify is uploaded into Perplexity
IF retention or deletion requirements differ between the two services
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Perplexity
Review both vendors’ retention settings
Document a data-flow map before use
Minimize logged content in Dify
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA and residency review
